ENT CLINICAL NOTE

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • 4-day history of sore throat progressing to dry cough; preceded by close exposure to a sneezing co-worker.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Day 1-2: painful sore throat, odynophagia, low-grade fever.  
  • Day 3-4: throat pain improving; new persistent dry cough and marked nasal congestion; ongoing runny nose now clearing; night sweats and fatigue; myalgias noted past 2 days.
- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat: initial odynophagia (pain on swallowing) for 1–2 days; no throat-tightening, no voice change, no drooling.  
  • Nose: persistent congestion, previously clear rhinorrhea.  
  • Ears: no otalgia, no fullness, no discharge, no hearing change.  
  • No facial, lip, tongue, or uvular swelling.  
  • No stridor, noisy breathing, or resting dyspnea (reports mild exertional shortness of breath only).  
  • No neck pain or swelling.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • None reported; has taken over-the-counter paracetamol and ibuprofen for fever/pain (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Drug/food/environmental allergies: none known.  
  • Current medications: paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented), ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Social context:
  • Lives alone; working as an accountant; continues to work but slower; plans time off as advised.

Objective:
- Observable swelling/distribution: none reported.
- Airway/breathing: patient reports normal breathing at rest; no mention of stridor or increased work of breathing.
- Mental status: alert; no dizziness or syncope reported.
- Vitals and physical examination findings: Not recorded (telehealth consult).
- Presence of another person with patient: lives alone; none present during call.

Assessment:
- Probable viral upper respiratory tract infection / early influenza with resolving pharyngitis and evolving dry cough and nasal congestion.
  • Justification: acute onset after exposure, typical viral symptom cluster (sore throat, rhinorrhea, fever, myalgias), improving course, absence of red-flag airway findings.

Plan:
- Immediate/advised actions:
  • Supportive care only: continue paracetamol and ibuprofen as needed for fever/pain; ensure adequate hydration and rest.
  • Recommend 1-2 days off work to facilitate recovery.
- Patient education / instructions:
  • Maintain good oral hydration, balanced nutrition as tolerated.  
  • Avoid strenuous activity until symptoms improve.
- Escalation criteria / red flags:
  • Seek urgent review if high fever returns, breathing becomes labored, chest pain develops, or symptoms persist beyond one week.  
  • Call clinic sooner if any new throat swelling, voice change, difficulty swallowing, or noisy breathing occurs.
- Follow-up:
  • Routine follow-up next week if no improvement or sooner if red-flag symptoms develop.  
  • No immediate ENT or allergy referral indicated at this stage.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing but clinically expected elements: objective vitals, direct oropharyngeal examination, chest examination, confirmed medication doses/frequencies, influenza/COVID testing status, vaccination status, formal allergy list despite “none known”.  
● Internal conflicts: none identified.  
● Transcript quality: clear; minimal background noise; complete history captured.
